This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $A=\{1\leq a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ and $B=\{1\leq b_1<b_2<\cdots\}$ be sets of integers with $a_n/b_n\to 1$. 
If $A+B$ contains all sufficiently large positive integers then is it true that $\limsup 1_A\ast 1_B(n)=\infty$?
#1145: [Va99,1.17]
additive combinatorics | 
additive basis
A conjecture of Erdős and Sárközy. Some condition relating $A$ and $B$ is necessary since, for example, if $A$ is the set of all integers with only even binary digits and $B$ is the set of all integers with only odd binary digits then $1_A\ast 1_B(n)=1$ for all $n$.
This is a stronger form of [28]. See also [331].
Additional thanks to: Felix Pernegger and Wouter van Doorn
